adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「く、なんてソフィスティケーテッドなバストなんだ……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Guh, why is this Busto so Sofistiketedo..."
comments: Continuing with Engrish... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Youko: "I don't, know at all... ah..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Aaaah.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺、誘惑されちゃってる。
adjudicated.en: I have been made prey of temptation.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: まんまと誘惑されちゃってる。
adjudicated.en: Artfully been made prey of temptation.
adjudicated.assessment: まんまと means that he has been thoroughly or neatly taken in. 'Artfully' attributes artistic skill to the unstated process rather than describing his complete capitulation.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "fWaaah～"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Senpai had awakened.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese reports that she woke up at this point. The past perfect incorrectly places the awakening before another past reference point.

adjudicated.jp: 「……いけない……眼鏡したまま寝て……寝て……」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "...unacceptable... sleeping while wearing glasses... sleeping..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺たちの痴態に目を留めた。
adjudicated.en: She took notice of our foolishness.
comments: And this is the absolutely first time ever in the whole of Cross Channel that anyone interacts with both Youko and Taichi... or do they? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 痴態 denotes the indecent or disgraceful spectacle before her. 'Foolishness' suppresses that specifically compromising quality.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "SE'YAH!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 手刀が振り下ろされた。
adjudicated.en: A hand chop swung downwards.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 乳首と指先を切断してのける。
adjudicated.en: It severs the contact between fingertip and udder.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that the chop severs contact between nipple and fingertip. 'Udder' replaces the human body part with an animal organ.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "Peke-kun!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ye-, yes!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「今のはイエロー停学ですから！」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "That now was a yellow suspension do you know!"
comments: RED SUSPENSION C'MON! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese comic disciplinary declaration is intelligible, but the English word order and unpunctuated tag are ungrammatical.

highlights.text: That now was a yellow suspension do you know!

adjudicated.jp: がっしと指を突きつけられる。
adjudicated.en: Snatch!, and she thrusts a finger at me.
comments: BTW: "gasshi", the (odd, undocumented) SFX used here, also means "to combine". Let's say it's a coincidence. Let's say that. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: レッド停学とかあるのかな……。
adjudicated.en: Could there be a red suspension I wonder...
comments: What you'd call a full mast? See CCA0003 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「し、しかしソフィスティケーテッドなおぱい子がですね！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "B-, but this here is a Sofistiketedo Bajungal!"
comments: Banjugas + gal, should be clear with the Bajungas Touch above. "おっぱいのでかい子" confirmed to be this http://ts.revinx.net/project/dic/crossc.htm -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese extends the preceding bad-English joke into a girl who wants to be urbanely sophisticated. The invented pseudo-loan compound does not preserve that recoverable meaning.

adjudicated.jp: 先輩は首を落とすような勇ましい仕草で、腕を薙いだ。
adjudicated.en: With a heroic gesture that reminds of the slaying of her enemy, Senpai scythed her arm sideways.
comments: It's a very chuuni gesture. And the very next line... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese compares the bold arm motion to cutting off a head; it does not introduce an enemy whose slaying she recalls.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "It has been a while, Hasekura-san."
comments: This is the absolute first time that any character has interacted with Youko and Taichi simultaneously. It is also the single and only line that Misato actually addresses at Youko throughout the entire scene. She's also changing in mood immediately and straightly, just like the similar scene in CCA0016. Right after a line chock full of chuuni. It can't be said it's not suspicious. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Youko: "...mh."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "Truly... owChChCh!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Are you all right?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ああ、なにやら資材が崩れてきて……」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Yes, for some reason the materials fell down on me..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「曜子ちゃんが助けてくれたんですよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Youko-chan has saved you you know."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "Oh... it was Hasekura-san?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Youko: "I was not the one who saved her, no."
comments: These two lines are not necessarily directed at each other... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Then who?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Youko: "...Shima Tomoki."
comments: ...as Misato has no reaction to her words... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "It was Tomoki?"
comments: ...but only when he and he repeats it out loud, so if she were to have said nothing, Misato would still hear this. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ははーん、それであいつさっき……。
adjudicated.en: Ah-hah, that is why that guy just earlier...
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「先輩、あいつ照れ屋なもんだから……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Senpai, that guy's really shy, so..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: みみ先輩は、呆然としていた。
adjudicated.en: Senpai was standing in blank amazement.
comments: And this'll be the least strange interaction with Taichi, Youko and someone else... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...hello?"
comments: She doesn't even seem to be 'here' anymore. Of course, metaphircally it fits - it's how she ignores the world, similarly to how everyone else does, one way or another. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "Tomoki has... me...?"
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese deliberately trails off after placing Tomoki and herself in relation. The English inserts 'has,' which creates an unintended transitive construction rather than preserving the open ellipsis.

adjudicated.jp: 狼狽しているようにも見える。
adjudicated.en: She also seems to be disconcerted.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: When did it even begin,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: この二人は、全く口をきかなくなったのだ。
adjudicated.en: the disappearance of any and all verbal contact between these two.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: In the club room Tomoki,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Senpai in the broadcast room.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 互いに同じ空間に居合わせることさえまれになった。
adjudicated.en: The mere mutual simultaneous presence of both in the same space became rarity.
adjudicated.assessment: The English count noun requires an article: their sharing the same space became a rarity.

adjudicated.jp: 誰が見ても、悟ることができた。
adjudicated.en: It was something that could be perceived by anyone who went and looked.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ただその理由だけが、秘められたままで。
adjudicated.en: Just that the reason for it, alone, they kept to themselves.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺たちの不和は、誰の間にもあったのだ。
adjudicated.en: Our discord was something that existed between anyone.
comments: OK, Japan, you will now hand over the brilliant mind who decided fuwa is also friction, or it's 不和不和 time. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that discord existed among every one of them. 'Between anyone' is ungrammatical and fails to express the group-wide distribution.

adjudicated.jp: 気がつくと曜子ちゃんは消えていた。
adjudicated.en: When I come to notice, Youko-chan had disappeared.
comments: As always, if she had never been there in the first place. Or, given Misato's refusal of noticing Taichi, maybe as if he was the one who left. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The surrounding narration is past-tense; the Japanese means 'when I noticed' or 'before I knew it,' not the malformed present-tense phrase.

withheld.jp: 「都会的に洗練されたい子のことなど理由にはなりません！」
withheld.en: Misato: "Being an urbanly refined Bajungal is not the kind of thing that can allowed as an excuse!"
comments: http://www.boobpedia.com/boobs/Alternate_names_for_breasts I can't even wonder WTF, I am too flabbergasted that this isn't a Japanese page -GHS
